question: Should Microsoft Teams officially support the proposed accounts/defaultAccount contract while retaining root-level single-bot configuration as an ongoing compatibility path?
rationale: This is a permanent public configuration, credential, setup, and state-ownership decision; tests can validate the implementation but cannot decide how much legacy surface the project intends to support.

options.title: Approve the additive contract
options.body: Accept accounts/defaultAccount with the documented root-level compatibility path, then resolve conflicts and require clean exact-head upgrade and fresh-install proof.

options.title: Require a migration-first shape
options.body: Define one canonical account-based shape and require an explicit doctor/setup migration plan before accepting the feature.

options.title: Defer multi-account Teams
options.body: Keep the canonical feature request open but pause or close this implementation until the long-term config and ownership contract is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve the additive contract
recommendation.body: Accept accounts/defaultAccount with the documented root-level compatibility path, then resolve conflicts and require clean exact-head upgrade and fresh-install proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans bundled-channel product direction, public config compatibility, setup behavior, credentials, and persistent state rather than a narrow Teams code repair.
